name: Guardian genius crossword No 197
preamble: ll vwls hv bn rmvd frm bth cls nd sltns.

solutions.check: grid and clues read from the Guardian's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; each light's entry one fifteensquared prints for it or the preamble's rule (vowels removed) makes of its answer, the only choice of them whose crossings all agree; an entry not its answer carries the answer as its alteration's `from`

clue.text: n brf: ’d gt t b rstlss

indicators.note: 'In' says the answer sits inside the following words, so it starts on the closing letter of the first of them

blocks.note: the run begins on the final letter of brief; that the printed consonants here spell the grid entry is no coincidence, being the same run with vowels gone
'I'd get' with its vowels restored, taken whole

explanation.surface: A short note saying the writer would end up restless.
explanation.walkthrough: With vowels this is a plain hidden word: 'In brief: I'd get to be restless', the answer running from the end of 'brief' through 'I'd get'.
explanation.definitionFit: To fidget is to make small restless movements, so it means to be restless.

clue.text: Lk blck stn pr

blocks.note: first meaning: 'Like black', as jet the black stone is
second meaning: 'stone pier', a landing stage built out into water

explanation.walkthrough: Read with vowels as 'Like black stone pier'; the answer is the adjective from jet and also the noun for a pier.
explanation.definitionFit: Jetty as an adjective means jet-black; as a noun it is a pier or landing stage.

clue.text: nttn shwn by Sssx Cnty pnrs pprng n tw ntrntnls

indicators.note: pioneers go first, so only the opening letters of the county words are used
'appearing in' places one set of letters inside the others

blocks.note: INT is the abbreviation for international, taken twice
the first letter of Sussex
the first letter of County

explanation.surface: Gut feeling displayed by early Sussex cricketers playing in a pair of international matches.
explanation.walkthrough: With vowels: 'Intuition shown by Sussex County pioneers appearing in two internationals'. S goes into the first INT and C into the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Instinct is a feeling known without reasoning, which is what intuition means.

clue.text: Cmpss ndr cnvs? n th cntrry!

indicators.note: 'on the contrary' asks for the opposite of the position the clue first states

blocks.note: 'under' canvas means in it; the opposite is out of it, and EX means out of
canvas is the stuff of a tent, and under canvas means in a tent

explanation.surface: Camping talk: is your range limited when sleeping in a tent? No, quite the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: With vowels: 'Compass under canvas? On the contrary!' Under canvas is in a tent, so its contrary is ex-tent.
explanation.definitionFit: Compass in the sense of range or scope is a synonym for extent.

clue.text: Hs pln n rns, pckng p frsh l pnt tht’s hndy

indicators.note: a plan in ruins is wrecked, so its letters are rebuilt in another order
picking up means holding another group of letters within
fresh signals the letters are made anew in a different order

blocks.note: 'His plan' taken as letters
'oil', which loses both its vowels in this puzzle

explanation.surface: A decorator's scheme collapses as he picks up a new oil paint that comes in handy.
explanation.walkthrough: With vowels: 'His plan in ruins, picking up fresh oil paint that's handy'. 'Handy' is the pun: the paint is for hands.
explanation.definitionFit: Nail polish is a lacquer painted on fingernails, so a paint for the hands.

clue.text: strt fllwng frc’s chf sspct

indicators.note: the chief of a word is its head, its opening letter
following puts the letters after the force piece rather than before it

blocks.note: the first letter of force
the clue began with the word 'I', which vanished entirely when the vowels were removed
to start, like a horse taking fright, is to shy

explanation.surface: A detective says he started following the police chief's main suspect.
explanation.walkthrough: The full clue is 'I, start following force's chief: suspect'. The opening 'I' is all vowel, so it disappears from the printed clue but still supplies a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fishy is dubious or questionable, which is what suspect means as an adjective.

clue.text: Rflctns frm fncy rn sd tbl

indicators.note: fancy means ornate or elaborated, so these letters are worked into a new arrangement

blocks.note: 'iron side table' with its vowels restored

explanation.surface: Mirror images seen in an ornate wrought-iron side table.
explanation.walkthrough: With vowels: 'Reflections from fancy iron side table'. 'Reflections' looks like images in a polished surface but means careful thoughts.
explanation.definitionFit: Reflections are careful considerations, which is what deliberations are.

clue.text: Rvrsd fnnc chrgs

blocks.note: to finance a venture is to back it
charges are people in someone's care, wards

explanation.surface: A report that finance charges have been cancelled.
explanation.walkthrough: With vowels: 'Reversed finance charges'. 'Charges' looks like fees but means people in one's care.
explanation.definitionFit: Something reversed runs the wrong way round, which is what backwards describes.

clue.text: Cttng Gds dd, xtrm fr-rght grp ldrs n ntrnl ngttns, yng Scts

indicators.note: 'leaders in' takes the front letter of each of the words that follow

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for dead
OTT, over the top, means extreme
the English Defence League, a British far-right group
the first letters of internal, negotiations, eyeing and Scouts

explanation.surface: A political report: gods dead, extremist leaders in internal talks, watched by Scouts.
explanation.walkthrough: With vowels: 'Cutting Guides dead, extreme far-right group leaders in internal negotiations, eyeing Scouts'. Initials come from the vowelled words, so 'yng' gives E for eyeing.
explanation.definitionFit: Dotted lines are printed guides showing where to cut a coupon or form.

clue.text: Cht 20

blocks.note: first meaning: to cheat or betray someone
second meaning: 20 in Roman numerals is XX, two crosses

explanation.walkthrough: With vowels: 'Cheat 20'. The number looks like a cross-reference to 20 Down, but it is the Roman numeral XX.
explanation.definitionFit: To double-cross is to betray or cheat a partner; XX is literally two crosses.

clue.text: Mrk’s wth ldy n vctn — tht’s xctng

indicators.note: on vacation the word is emptied of its inside, keeping only its ends

blocks.note: a tick is a mark on a page
the outside letters of lady

explanation.surface: Mark is off on holiday with a lady, which sounds thrilling.
explanation.walkthrough: With vowels: 'Mark's with lady on vacation — that's exciting'. Mark looks like a man's name but is a tick.
explanation.definitionFit: Tickly describes a tingling, ticklish sensation, the physical sense of exciting the nerves.

clue.text: Rcnstrctd tln scllry n n nthntc fshn

indicators.note: reconstructed means rebuilt, so the letters are put together again differently

blocks.note: 'Italian scullery' with its vowels restored

explanation.surface: A rebuilt Italian kitchen done up in a fake, not-quite-genuine style.
explanation.walkthrough: With vowels: 'Reconstructed Italian scullery in an inauthentic fashion'. The vowelless fodder hides how many vowels the answer has.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something unrealistically means doing it in a way that is not true to life.

clue.text: Blk tks vr nd strts t nmnt mnstrs — thy rn th cntry

indicators.note: the bloke takes letters into himself, holding them inside
'starts to' takes only the opening letter of each following word

blocks.note: a bloke is a man, a gent
'over', reduced to two consonants
the first letters of nominate and ministers

explanation.surface: A man takes charge and begins naming his cabinet, who will run the country.
explanation.walkthrough: With vowels: 'Bloke takes over and starts to nominate ministers — they run the country'. 'Takes over' looks like a phrase but splits into container and contents.
explanation.definitionFit: The government is the body of people who administer the state.

clue.text: nvs Chgwll smpltn bng cptvtd by prttsts

indicators.note: something captivated is held captive, enclosed by other letters

blocks.note: Gilbert and Sullivan, the operetta writers, are G and S
Barnaby Rudge, Dickens's simple-minded hero, lives in Chigwell

explanation.surface: A village idiot from Chigwell is jealous after being charmed by opera singers.
explanation.walkthrough: With vowels: 'Envies Chigwell simpleton being captivated by operettists'. Chigwell is an Essex village and the setting of Dickens's Barnaby Rudge.
explanation.definitionFit: To grudge someone something is to resent their having it, which is to envy them.

clue.text: Mthr tks n rl prfrmng wth dghtr n snstnl thtrcs

'role', stripped of its vowels
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A mother accepts a stage part alongside her daughter in an overblown drama.
explanation.walkthrough: With vowels: 'Mother takes on role performing with daughter in sensational theatrics'.
explanation.definitionFit: Melodrama is drama with exaggerated, sensational emotion, which is what overdone theatrics are.

clue.text: Bts th lngst pssbl nchngng wrd!

blocks.note: first meaning: beats, regular patterns of sound
second meaning: in this puzzle a word with no vowels is unchanged, and this is the longest such word

explanation.walkthrough: With vowels: 'Beats the longest possible unchanging word!' It is the one entry that survives the vowel removal intact, being the longest common English word without A, E, I, O or U.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhythms are regular beats in music or speech, so the plural fits the plural beats.

clue.text: n’s sd by prts’ swshbcklng rchtyp, lttng t shtd ‘rr’!

indicators.note: swashbuckling is wild and flamboyant, so the letters are thrown about
letting out means releasing, so a letter is let go from the word
shouted means spoken out loud, so the sound counts rather than the spelling

blocks.note: 'archetype' with its vowels back
the pirate's cry 'arr' is said like the letter R

explanation.surface: The classic swashbuckling pirate, crying 'arr!', uses one of these.
explanation.walkthrough: With vowels: 'One's used by pirates' swashbuckling archetype, letting out shouted arr!' Drop one R from archetype and rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyepatch covering one eye is a stock accessory of the stage pirate.

clue.text: ntrnc, bng cptvtd by sng n th lps, mvng wth rglr 14

indicators.note: only what is on the lips, the outer edges of the word, is kept
captivated means held captive, enclosed by other letters

blocks.note: 'snog', a British word for a long kiss, keeps only its outside letters
a way in is an entrance

explanation.surface: A doorway charmed by a kiss on the lips, moving to a regular beat.
explanation.walkthrough: With vowels: 'Entrance, being captivated by snog on the lips, moving with regular 14'. 14 refers to the answer RHYTHMS; snog is British slang for a kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: Swaying is moving rhythmically from side to side, so moving with regular rhythms.

clue.text: Mdfd jd std?

indicators.note: something modified is altered, so the letters are changed round

blocks.note: 'jade stud' with its vowels restored

explanation.surface: An earring, a green jade stud, that has been altered.
explanation.walkthrough: With vowels: 'Modified jade stud?' The one word serves as both definition and anagram signal, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjusted means altered slightly, a direct synonym of modified.

clue.text: Bld r cn n cr bgnnng t vrpwr s

indicators.note: 'in' places the air con letters inside the car
'beginning to' takes only the first letter of the next word

blocks.note: an Audi is a make of car
air con, air conditioning, is AC
the first letter of overpower
'us', reduced to S without its vowel

explanation.surface: Brave of the air conditioning in the car, starting to overwhelm us.
explanation.walkthrough: With vowels: 'Bold air con in car beginning to overpower us'. Here a two-letter word 'us' is left as the single letter S.
explanation.definitionFit: Audacious means daring and fearless, the sense of bold applied to people and actions.

clue.text: Gttng nnyd, ’d try St Cstrd’s — pst, thy xprss dspprvl

St Custard's is Nigel Molesworth's school, which he spells skool

explanation.surface: Irritated, I'd attempt a famous boarding school, but past pupils frown on it.
explanation.walkthrough: With vowels: 'Getting annoyed, I'd try St Custard's — past, they express disapproval'. St Custard's is the school in the Molesworth books, a British comic classic.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirty looks are glares that signal disapproval without words.

clue.text: Grnd shlld mtrpls, csng trg

indicators.note: shelled means stripped of its shell, its outermost letters

blocks.note: 'go round' on watch is to patrol
a metropolis is a large city

explanation.surface: A city is shelled and the bombardment of the capital causes outrage.
explanation.walkthrough: With vowels: 'Go round shelled, metropolis, causing outrage'. Shelled looks like bombardment but means peeled.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrocity is a shocking, cruel act, an outrage in the noun sense.

clue.text: Rqst t rtrn t th stg lft bhnd brkn cn cntnng prn? Qt th rvrs!

definitions.text: Rqst t rtrn t th stg

indicators.note: something broken is smashed up, so its letters are put back differently
containing places one word within another
'quite the reverse' swaps which word holds which, so the second holds the first

blocks.note: to prune is to cut back, to curtail
'can', reduced to its consonants
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A plea to come back on stage, ending with a dented tin with a prune inside, or the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: With vowels: 'Request to return to the stage: left behind broken can containing prune? Quite the reverse!' The prune word holds the jumbled can, and L follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A curtain call is the audience's applause summoning performers back to take a bow.

clue.text: Rvwd tln rd: n th ns, tnnn; t th fnsh, plm nd lych — n nplsnt mxtr

the first letter of tannin
the last letter of plum

the last letters of an and unpleasant

explanation.surface: A wine critic's note on an Italian red: tannic on the nose, plum and lychee on the finish, and nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: With vowels: 'Reviewed Italian red: in the nose, tannin; at the finish, plum and lychee — an unpleasant mixture'. Nose and finish are wine-tasting terms for the start and end.
explanation.definitionFit: An assortment is a varied collection of things, a mixture.

clue.text: Prvrt dmrd sn — tht’s t f rdr

explanation.walkthrough: With vowels: 'Pervert admired son — that's out of order'. Out of order sounds like disapproval but is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Randomised things are placed in no particular sequence, without any arrangement.

clue.text: Wntng t mv pg rnd, s mny mplyng brbrn

a Hun is a barbarian

explanation.surface: A man keen to relocate a pig, using money to hire a barbarian.
explanation.walkthrough: With vowels: 'Wanting to move: pig round, use money employing barbarian'. Tin for money is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: House-hunting is looking for a new home, which is what someone wanting to move does.

clue.text: Shtng’s lttl grtng?

explanation.surface: A question whether shouting at someone is a mild form of insult.
explanation.walkthrough: With vowels: 'Shouting's little grating?' Grating looks like an adjective for irritating but is the noun for a grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Heckling is interrupting a speaker with shouted jeers.

clue.text: Whr nmbrs g wtht stppng

blocks.note: first meaning: where numbers go, the hours on a clock face
second meaning: without stopping, all day and night

explanation.walkthrough: With vowels: 'Where numbers go without stopping'. It reads as one phrase but splits into two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The numerals on a clock are placed around its face; working around the clock means continuously.

clue.text: ncvr rg strn

blocks.note: a rogue is a scoundrel, a wretch

explanation.surface: Exposing a villain puts a strain on the investigator.
explanation.walkthrough: With vowels: 'Uncover rogue strain'.
explanation.definitionFit: To retch is to strain as if to vomit, the convulsive effort without bringing anything up.

clue.text: Lk th dvl thr sd f Hllw’n, b brndd n th tl

'in the tail' keeps the final letter of each word

either ... or, so 'either' calls up OR
the last letters of be and branded

explanation.surface: Like the devil at Halloween, a costume branded on the tail.
explanation.walkthrough: With vowels: 'Like the devil either side of Hallowe'en, be branded in the tail'.
explanation.definitionFit: The devil is pictured with horns, so horned describes him.

clue.text: Gm fr th dtr t spprt n pch

explanation.walkthrough: With vowels: 'Game for the auditor to support one peach'. Auditor looks like an accountant but means a listener; peach is an old verb for informing.
explanation.definitionFit: Baccarat is a card game played in casinos.

clue.text: Lths sslt crs wtht lmts (nt fr vryn)

indicators.note: without limits means with both its boundary letters removed

'course' without its vowels

explanation.walkthrough: With vowels: 'Loathes assault course without limits (not for everyone)'. Course loses its ends, then the U (the universal film rating) goes too.
explanation.definitionFit: To abhor is to regard with disgust and hatred, which is to loathe.

clue.text: Fthr n TV dscrbng hrs wth mrk n

explanation.walkthrough: With vowels: 'Father on TV describing a horse with mark on'. The 'a' disappears from the printed clue but still supplies its letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tagged has a label or marker attached to it.

clue.text: Tch chld wrkrs — thy’r ll y’r sng t th mmnt!

explanation.walkthrough: With vowels: 'Teach child workers — they're all you're seeing at the moment!' The definition describes this very puzzle, whose clues show only consonants.
explanation.definitionFit: With every vowel removed, consonants are the only letters left on show in these clues.

clue.text: Sld cl fr ‘nrv’

blocks.note: surface reading: a sound, sturdy clue whose solution is the word nerve
setter's reading: the answer itself, read as a clue, is a jumble instruction whose letters rearrange into nerve

explanation.walkthrough: With vowels: 'Solid clue for nerve'. Treat the answer as a cryptic clue: the first word is the fodder and the second its signal, producing 'nerve'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something never-failing is dependable and reliable, which is the sense of solid here.
